dppca: Differentially Private Principal Component Analysis Visualization

Source: R/dppca-package.R
dppca-package.Rd

Tools for estimating principal component directions and constructing differentially private PCA visualizations. The package provides private principal component directions; clipped, modified-winsorized, and Huber scree and proportion-of-variance-explained summaries; additive and sparse two-dimensional score histograms; group-wise score visualizations; synthetic score sampling from released private histograms; and an interactive Shiny application.

Details

dp_pca() stores a shared set of private estimates for summaries and scree, score, loading, variable, and biplot displays. Its default settings disable sample-mean centering and omit non-private reference results. dp_loading(), dp_scree(), and dp_score() also support print, summary and plot methods for their stored results. For example, call dp_loading() with a privacy budget, then plot the fit. The Shiny app also supports diagnostic comparisons that include non-private data summaries.

Data frames may include numeric and non-numeric columns. PCA uses the numeric feature columns and warns when non-numeric columns are excluded. Set group to a column name in dp_score() or dp_pca() to obtain grouped score results; the selected group column is excluded from the PCA features, even when it is numeric. Leave group = NULL for an ungrouped analysis. Summaries identify the selected group variable and its groups. Numeric features are used without automatic centering or standardization. See the individual functions for preprocessing assumptions and privacy-budget accounting.
